title: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation
claim: Prior methods supervise each transition with only one goal's target; ours supervises all goals at once, sharing one critic representation.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right; stacked method comparison, then two contrasting dashed-divided diagrams
description: The figure has three panels separated by dashed vertical lines. Panel (a), on the left, shows five robot-kitchen thumbnails labeled g1 to g5, with g3 highlighted. Under them are three stacked rounded boxes: gray for HGC, purple for iHGC, and green for VaDar. Each box has a row of pink goal-index cells, plus blue policy and orange Q-function boxes joined by arrows. A red X marks the removed policy conditioning in iHGC. Panel (b) is a purple box showing (s,a) feeding a shared-representation grid, with arrows to goals g1 through gK. Only g1 is highlighted, and the rest are faded. Panel (c) is a green box with the same grid, but all goals are active and bold arrows return to the shared representation. Red text and dashed arrows say that all goals update the same shared representation.
caption: \Vadar{} uses subgoals during training but requires none at deployment. (a) \hgc{} conditions both policy and critic on the current subgoal; \ihgc{} removes policy conditioning. \Vadar{} adds all-subgoal critic supervision and future-aware policy extraction. (b) With single-goal supervision, each transition supplies a TD target for only the current subgoal. (c) \Vadar{} supervises all subgoals on each transition, updating a shared critic representation. We hypothesize that this enables an implicit Bellman backup that improves final-goal value estimates.
abstract: Long-horizon tasks are important for modern AI and robotics, yet pose a challenge for reinforcement learning. Historically, a popular approach has been to decompose a task into subgoals, and learn a subgoal-conditioned policy to execute each subtask in sequence. We introduce an alternative called Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values. Because subgoal information is needed only at training-time, VaDar removes the need for possibly costly or cumbersome subgoal-selection during policy deployment. Moreover, through careful experiments, we show that VaDar (1) is always competitive with, and frequently outperforms, natural baselines like goal-conditioning and (2) succeeds on tasks with non-sequential goal structure and multiple optimization objectives. In particular, VaDar is the first algorithm to solve challenging, long-horizon tasks in the RoboCasa suite, even when starting from a policy pretrained from behavior cloning with near-zero initial task success. Taken together, VaDar's successes suggest that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.
